policy: No novelty claim without literature review, and before publication or patenting, a patent/prior-art review. An entry may only be marked REVIEWED when it actually cites related work. Every hypothesis in pocketsec.stage0.hypotheses must appear here.

entries.claim: A conventional compact classifier / GRU is an adequate hard baseline for Linux security-event sequences.
entries.notes: No novelty claimed: H0 is deliberately prior art. Review needed only to pick a defensible representative, not to establish originality.

entries.claim: A state-space / recurrent baseline captures temporal structure at fixed state cost.
entries.notes: No novelty claimed. Survey S4/Mamba-family and classical HMM literature before selecting a representative.

entries.claim: Security behaviour can be compiled into a minimal learned automaton over states and transitions.
entries.notes: Overlaps heavily with automata learning, grammatical inference and state minimisation. Stage 1 added ordered capability lattices and a compositional Φ; both are conventional constructions and NO novelty is claimed. Must be reviewed before any novelty language is used anywhere in the project.

entries.claim: Computation can be budgeted by informational surprise so cost scales with novelty rather than event volume.
entries.notes: Adjacent to conditional computation, early-exit networks and adaptive computation time. Instrumented in ThreatPredictionV1.compute_path, but the mechanism is unmeasured at Stage 0.

entries.claim: Stable learned behaviour can be JIT-compiled into cheap executable detectors, and demoted back when it degrades.
entries.notes: Adjacent to neural-to-symbolic rule extraction, knowledge distillation and model compilation. The reversible demotion path is the part most worth checking for prior art.

entries.claim: Model complexity can follow host behavioural complexity via adaptive state growth and merging.
entries.notes: Adjacent to non-parametric Bayesian methods, dynamic architectures and state-merging automata induction.

entries.claim: A HOT/WARM/COLD/FORGOTTEN hierarchy bounds memory while retaining recognisable behaviour.
entries.notes: Adjacent to cache hierarchies, sketching/sublinear summaries and continual-learning replay buffers.

entries.claim: A relational latent state over process/user/file/network entities beats raw event-sequence representation.
entries.notes: Substantial existing work in provenance-graph intrusion detection. Stage 1 implements a relational entity/relation encoding (SSIR) plus a lineage-scoped state calculus; NO novelty is claimed for either. Review before any comparative claim. See ADR-0005, ADR-0006.

entries.claim: The combined NERA architecture outperforms its parts, with each component independently justified by ablation.
entries.notes: Stage 0 non-goal is explicit: do not claim NERA is novel or superior. This entry stays NOT_REVIEWED until the component hypotheses have measured ablations.
